newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League player Stephen Kernahan told South Australian selectors last night that he would be unavailable for Saturday night's State of Origin match against Victoria. Kernahan, who was expected to captain the side if selected, is suffering lingering soreness from a groin strain. At the age of 33 it seems unlikely Kernahan will play for the State side again. Page 20.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker said yesterday that it was time to define rugby league's future for the supporters and the clubs. Super League welcomed the comments, but Super League would not comment on whether talks were imminent, with both sides recognising the need for one competition. Page 20.

The National Basketball League's executive board meeting today is expected to discuss the decision to play a 30-game regular season schedule in the interim season next year. Clubs that own their own venues would financially benefit from the 30-game season but others would prefer only 20 games. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Two Australian tennis players have been seeded at Wimbledon for the first time in 15 years. Queen's champion Mark Philippoussis has been seeded seventh and French Open semi-finalist Pat Rafter is seeded twelfth, and will not play any of the favoured players until the fourth round. Page 48.

Australian Jockey Club stipendiary stewards' deputy chairman Jamie Stier has found bottles that normally contain multivitamins for horses were laced with a prohibited substance, and stewards' chairman Ray Murrihy has warned trainers not to use the product. Three irregularities have been found in samples from horses so far. Page 49.

Australian cricket pace bowler Paul Reiffel has replaced the injured Jason Gillespie in the Australian side to meet England at the Lord's Cricket Ground for the second Ashes Test match starting today. Australian captain Mark Taylor is confident, and said the mood and preparation for this Test were better than for the first Test. Page 50.
THE AGE

Leading jockey Greg Childs rode The Stash to a length-and-a-quarter win in the Nearest Handicap (1,400 metres) at Sandown yesterday, but lost the race after stewards upheld Craig Williams' protest of interference on his horse Kenvite over the last 300 metes. Page C18.

The Court of Appeal has retired to consider its decision on the future of Carlton Australian Football League centre-man Greg Williams. The AFL appealed against a Supreme Court ruling that overturned the AFL Tribunal's nine week suspension of Williams for interfering with an umpire. Page C18.

The operation to repair Australian Football League player Gary Lyon's back has gone smoothly and the Melbourne captain could be out of hospital within days. The operation repaired damage to a disc in Lyon's lower back and made more room for the spinal nerves that come out of the cord. Page C18.
THE HERALD SUN

Hawthorn Australian Football League president Ian Dicker said last night the AFL had lost control of setting admission prices to games. Dicker said fans had to pay A$27.50 to see Hawthorn's game last weekend and could pay as much as A$44 for a premium sea at the Sydney Cricket Ground, well over the standard A$12.50 admission. Page 85.

Victoria's biggest horse racing trainers have formed an alliance with the Australian Workers Union to crack down on stable award cheats, due to the belief that the non-payment of award wages to stable staff is widespread and having an adverse effect on racing. Page 80.

Former Illawarra Hawk basketball player Marcus Timmons is training with the Melbourne Tigers team today, seeking the vacancy left by the weekend axing of import Jarvis Lang. Timmons played for Hawks in 1996 and was visiting friends in Australia when he got the call-up. Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Brisbane Broncos Super League coach Wayne Bennett has warned forward Gorden Tallis there would be no place for him in the team if there was a repeat of Monday night's violence. Tallis repeatedly punched Wigan forward Terry O'Connor, and received a warning from Super League commissioner Jim Hall. Page 87.

New South Wales surfers dominated the fourth day of competition in the Quiksilver Australian Junior Titles at Yallingup in south-west West Australia yesterday. Zane Harrison and Grant Hudson are through to Saturday's under 18 men's final and John Barnes and Adrian Bucan are through to the under 16 cadet boys division. Page 86.

The thoroughbred, harness and greyhound racing industries met yesterday to resolve the issues surrounding the privatisation of the New South Wales TAB early next year.The harness and greyhound industries could not agree on the way the final proportion of TAB funds should be distributed, and will seek independent mediation to break the deadlock. Page 78.
